standard_text: Area of triangles, parallelograms, and trapezoids
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 math worksheets on area for the BC curriculum: parallelograms (A = b × h), triangles (A = b × h ÷ 2), trapezoids (A = (a + b) ÷ 2 × h), composite shapes, and word problems about gardens, sails and flags. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Parallelogram: b × h. Triangle: b × h ÷ 2. Trapezoid: (a + b) ÷ 2 × h.
key_sub: The height meets the base at a right angle; a slanted side is not the height. Two copies of a triangle or a trapezoid make a parallelogram, so each one is half of it. Split composite shapes into rectangles and triangles, then add. Area is in square units (cm², m²).
body_html:
The big idea: start from the rectangle

You know the area of a rectangle: base × height. Parallelograms, triangles and trapezoids can all be cut apart or doubled to make a rectangle or a parallelogram. The height is always measured at a right angle to the base. It is shown as a dashed line with a small square at the corner.

Parallelograms: A = b × h

Cut the triangle off one end and slide it to the other end. The parallelogram becomes a rectangle with the same base and the same height. A rhombus is a parallelogram too.

Triangles: A = b × h ÷ 2

Two copies of any triangle make a parallelogram with the same base and height, so a triangle is half of it. In a right triangle, the two sides that meet at the right angle are the base and the height.

In a triangle with an obtuse angle, the height can fall outside the triangle. Extend the base with a dashed line and measure the height to that line.

Trapezoids: A = (a + b) ÷ 2 × h

A trapezoid has two parallel sides, a and b. Add them, divide by 2, then multiply by the height. Why? Two copies of the trapezoid make a parallelogram with base a + b, and the trapezoid is half of it.

Check by cutting

Use the same trapezoid. Cut it into a rectangle and two triangles.

Rectangle: 8 × 8 = 64. The triangles’ bases add up to 20 − 8 = 12, so together they are 12 × 8 ÷ 2 = 48. Add: 64 + 48 = 112.

Answer: 112 cm², the same as the formula

Composite shapes: split or subtract

Split the shape into rectangles and triangles that do not overlap, then add their areas. Or start with a big rectangle and subtract the piece that is missing.

Subtract a piece

A 10 m by 8 m rectangle has a triangle cut out. The triangle has a base of 8 m and a height of 3 m. Find the area left.

Rectangle: 10 × 8 = 80. Triangle: 8 × 3 ÷ 2 = 12. Subtract: 80 − 12 = 68.

Answer: 68 m²

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using the slanted side as the heightUse the dashed height at a right angle to the base
Triangle: 14 × 12 = 168Divide by 2: 14 × 12 ÷ 2 = 84
Parallelogram: 12 × 8 ÷ 2 = 48No ÷ 2 for a parallelogram: 12 × 8 = 96
Trapezoid: (20 + 8) × 8 = 224Divide by 2: (20 + 8) ÷ 2 × 8 = 112
Counting a corner twice in an L-shapeSplit into pieces that do not overlap
Writing 84 m for an areaArea is in square units: 84 m²

faq.q: What do Grade 6 students learn about area in the BC math curriculum?
faq.a: In Geometry and measurement, Grade 6 students find the area of triangles, parallelograms and trapezoids by relating them to rectangles, and use these areas to solve problems, including composite shapes.

faq.q: Why do you divide by 2 to find the area of a triangle?
faq.a: Two copies of the same triangle fit together to make a parallelogram with the same base and height. The triangle is half of it, so its area is base × height ÷ 2.

faq.q: What is the formula for the area of a trapezoid?
faq.a: A = (a + b) ÷ 2 × h, where a and b are the parallel sides and h is the height. Two copies of the trapezoid make a parallelogram with base a + b, and the trapezoid is half of it.

faq.q: Is the slanted side the height of a parallelogram or triangle?
faq.a: No. The height is the distance straight across, at a right angle to the base. A slanted side is always longer than the height, so using it gives an area that is too big.

items.q: Cut along the dashed height and slide the triangle to the other end of the parallelogram. What rectangle do you get?
items.e: The base stays 14 cm and the height stays 8 cm, so the rectangle is 14 cm by 8 cm. That is why the parallelogram’s area is b × h = 14 × 8 = 112 cm².

items.q: A parallelogram has a base of 14 cm and a height of 11.5 cm. What is its area?
items.e: A = base × height = 14 × 11.5 = 161 cm². Do not divide by 2: a parallelogram is a rectangle with one end cut off and moved.

items.q: A parallelogram has an area of 135 cm². Its height is 9 cm. How long is its base?
items.e: Area = base × height, so ? × 9 = 135. 135 ÷ 9 = 15 cm. Check: 15 × 9 = 135.

items.q: A parallelogram has a base of 8.5 m and a height of 6 m. What is its area?
items.e: A = base × height = 8.5 × 6 = 51 m². Do not divide by 2: a parallelogram is a rectangle with one end cut off and moved.

items.q: This rhombus has four sides of 13 mm. What is its area?
items.e: A rhombus is a parallelogram, so A = base × height = 13 × 12 = 156 mm². 13 × 13 uses a slanted side, not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 14 × 12 = 168 cm². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 13 cm side.

items.q: Which expression gives the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: Area = base × height = 11 × 12 = 132 cm². 15 is the slanted side, ÷ 2 is for triangles, and 2 × (11 + 15) is the perimeter.

items.q: A parallelogram has an area of 96 m². Its base is 12 m. What is its height?
items.e: Area = base × height, so 12 × ? = 96. 96 ÷ 12 = 8 m. Check: 12 × 8 = 96.

items.q: Which expression gives the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: Area = base × height = 15 × 12 = 180 m². 13 is the slanted side, ÷ 2 is for triangles, and 2 × (15 + 13) is the perimeter.

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 16 × 6 = 96 m². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 10 m side.

items.q: Cut along the dashed height and slide the triangle to the other end of the parallelogram. What rectangle do you get?
items.e: The base stays 10 m and the height stays 12 m, so the rectangle is 10 m by 12 m. That is why the parallelogram’s area is b × h = 10 × 12 = 120 m².

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 9 × 8 = 72 m². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 10 m side. (Cut off the triangle at one end and slide it to the other end: you get a rectangle that is 9 by 8.)

items.q: A rectangle is 9 cm by 6 cm. A parallelogram has a base of 9 cm, a height of 6 cm and slanted sides of 7.5 cm. How do their areas compare?
c: The parallelogram is half as large.
items.e: Rectangle: 9 × 6 = 54 cm². Parallelogram: base × height = 9 × 6 = 54 cm². Same base and same height give the same area. (9 × 7.5 = 67.5 uses the slanted side.)

items.q: A parallelogram has a base of 7.5 m and a height of 4.2 m. What is its area?
items.e: A = base × height = 7.5 × 4.2 = 31.5 m². Do not divide by 2: a parallelogram is a rectangle with one end cut off and moved.

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 8 × 3 = 24 cm². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 5 cm side.

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 16 × 9 = 144 mm². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 15 mm side.

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 9 × 4 = 36 cm². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 5 cm side. (Cut off the triangle at one end and slide it to the other end: you get a rectangle that is 9 by 4.)

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 17 × 12 = 204 cm². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 15 cm side.

items.q: This rhombus has four sides of 10 m. What is its area?
items.e: A rhombus is a parallelogram, so A = base × height = 10 × 8 = 80 m². 10 × 10 uses a slanted side, not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 12 × 15 = 180 mm². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 17 mm side. (Cut off the triangle at one end and slide it to the other end: you get a rectangle that is 12 by 15.)

items.q: What is the area of the triangle?
items.e: The height is the dashed line: it meets the base at a right angle. A = base × height ÷ 2 = 27 × 18 ÷ 2 = 486 ÷ 2 = 243 cm². The 22.5 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the triangle?
items.e: The height is the dashed line: it meets the base at a right angle. A = base × height ÷ 2 = 12 × 15 ÷ 2 = 180 ÷ 2 = 90 m². The 25 m side is slanted, so it is not the height. This triangle has an obtuse angle, so its height falls outside it and meets the grey dashed extension of the base.

items.q: A diagonal cuts this rectangle into two equal triangles. What is the area of the shaded triangle?
items.e: The rectangle is 8 × 5 = 40 mm². The shaded triangle is half of it: 40 ÷ 2 = 20 mm².

items.q: A parallelogram and a triangle have the same base (14 cm) and the same height (9 cm). The parallelogram’s area is 126 cm². What is the triangle’s area?
items.e: Two copies of the triangle make a parallelogram with the same base and height, so the triangle is half of it: 126 ÷ 2 = 63 cm². Check: 14 × 9 ÷ 2 = 126 ÷ 2 = 63.

items.q: A triangle has a base of 7.5 m and a height of 4 m. What is its area?
items.e: A = 7.5 × 4 ÷ 2 = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 m². Do not forget to divide by 2: a triangle is half of a parallelogram.

items.q: Which expression gives the area of the triangle?
items.e: The base is 19 m. The height is the dashed 12 m line, which meets the base line at a right angle outside the triangle. A = 19 × 12 ÷ 2 = 114 m².

items.q: Which expression gives the area of the triangle?
items.e: The base is 6 cm. The height is the dashed 20 cm line, which meets the base line at a right angle outside the triangle. A = 6 × 20 ÷ 2 = 60 cm².

items.q: What is the area of the right triangle?
items.e: The two sides that meet at the right angle are the base and the height. A = 3 × 4 ÷ 2 = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 m². The 5 m side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: A triangle has a base of 15 cm and a height of 8.4 cm. What is its area?
items.e: A = 15 × 8.4 ÷ 2 = 126 ÷ 2 = 63 cm². Do not forget to divide by 2: a triangle is half of a parallelogram.

items.q: What is the area of the triangle?
items.e: The height is the dashed line: it meets the base at a right angle. A = base × height ÷ 2 = 24 × 9 ÷ 2 = 216 ÷ 2 = 108 cm². The 15 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the triangle?
items.e: The height is the dashed line: it meets the base at a right angle. A = base × height ÷ 2 = 7 × 12 ÷ 2 = 84 ÷ 2 = 42 m². The 20 m side is slanted, so it is not the height. This triangle has an obtuse angle, so its height falls outside it and meets the grey dashed extension of the base.

items.q: A triangle has an area of 42 m². Its height is 7 m. What is its base?
items.e: 7 × ? ÷ 2 = 42. Double the area first: 42 × 2 = 84. Then 84 ÷ 7 = 12 m. Check: 7 × 12 ÷ 2 = 84 ÷ 2 = 42 m².

items.q: What is the area of the triangle?
items.e: The height is the dashed line: it meets the base at a right angle. A = base × height ÷ 2 = 30 × 12 ÷ 2 = 360 ÷ 2 = 180 cm². The 37 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height. This triangle has an obtuse angle, so its height falls outside it and meets the grey dashed extension of the base.

items.q: What is the area of the right triangle?
items.e: The two sides that meet at the right angle are the base and the height. A = 10 × 24 ÷ 2 = 240 ÷ 2 = 120 mm². The 26 mm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: A triangle has a base of 12 cm and a height of 6.5 cm. What is its area?
items.e: A = 12 × 6.5 ÷ 2 = 78 ÷ 2 = 39 cm². Do not forget to divide by 2: a triangle is half of a parallelogram.

items.q: What is the area of the triangle?
items.e: The height is the dashed line: it meets the base at a right angle. A = base × height ÷ 2 = 7 × 6 ÷ 2 = 42 ÷ 2 = 21 mm². The 7.5 mm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the right triangle?
items.e: The two sides that meet at the right angle are the base and the height. A = 8 × 6 ÷ 2 = 48 ÷ 2 = 24 cm². The 10 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: A diagonal cuts this rectangle into two equal triangles. What is the area of the shaded triangle?
items.e: The rectangle is 12 × 7 = 84 m². The shaded triangle is half of it: 84 ÷ 2 = 42 m².

items.q: What is the area of the right triangle?
items.e: The two sides that meet at the right angle are the base and the height. A = 24 × 18 ÷ 2 = 432 ÷ 2 = 216 cm². The 30 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: A triangle has an area of 36 cm². Its base is 9 cm. What is its height?
items.e: 9 × ? ÷ 2 = 36. Double the area first: 36 × 2 = 72. Then 72 ÷ 9 = 8 cm. Check: 9 × 8 ÷ 2 = 72 ÷ 2 = 36 cm².

items.q: A trapezoid has an area of 60 m². Its parallel sides are 7 m and 5 m. What is its height?
What is the area of the trapezoid?
items.e: The parallel sides are 14 cm and 8 cm, and the height is 9 cm. A = (a + b) ÷ 2 × h = (14 + 8) ÷ 2 × 9 = 22 ÷ 2 × 9 = 11 × 9 = 99 cm². Do not forget to divide by 2.

items.q: Which expression gives the area of the trapezoid?
items.e: Add the two parallel sides, divide by 2, then multiply by the height: (18 + 8) ÷ 2 × 12 = 156 cm². The 13 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: A trapezoid has parallel sides of 8.4 m and 5.6 m. The height is 5 m. What is its area?
items.e: A = (a + b) ÷ 2 × h = (8.4 + 5.6) ÷ 2 × 5 = 14 ÷ 2 × 5 = 7 × 5 = 35 m². Add the parallel sides first, then halve, then multiply by the height.

items.q: A trapezoid has parallel sides of 10.5 cm and 5.5 cm. The height is 7 cm. What is its area?
items.e: A = (a + b) ÷ 2 × h = (10.5 + 5.5) ÷ 2 × 7 = 16 ÷ 2 × 7 = 8 × 7 = 56 cm². Add the parallel sides first, then halve, then multiply by the height.

items.q: What is the area of the trapezoid?
items.e: The parallel sides are 8 mm and 4 mm, and the height is 10 mm. A = (a + b) ÷ 2 × h = (8 + 4) ÷ 2 × 10 = 12 ÷ 2 × 10 = 6 × 10 = 60 mm². Do not forget to divide by 2.

items.q: The dashed lines cut the trapezoid into a rectangle and two triangles. What is its area?
items.e: Rectangle: 6 × 3 = 18 m². Triangles together: base 14 − 6 = 8 m, height 3 m, so 8 × 3 ÷ 2 = 24 ÷ 2 = 12 m². Add: 18 + 12 = 30 m². The formula gives the same answer: (14 + 6) ÷ 2 × 3 = 20 ÷ 2 × 3 = 10 × 3 = 30 m².

items.q: What is the area of the trapezoid?
items.e: The parallel sides are 18 cm and 6 cm, and the height is 8 cm. A = (a + b) ÷ 2 × h = (18 + 6) ÷ 2 × 8 = 24 ÷ 2 × 8 = 12 × 8 = 96 cm². The 10 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: The dashed lines cut the trapezoid into a rectangle and a triangle. What is its area?
items.e: Rectangle: 7 × 6 = 42 cm². Triangle: base 13 − 7 = 6 cm, height 6 cm, so 6 × 6 ÷ 2 = 36 ÷ 2 = 18 cm². Add: 42 + 18 = 60 cm². The formula gives the same answer: (13 + 7) ÷ 2 × 6 = 20 ÷ 2 × 6 = 10 × 6 = 60 cm².

items.q: What is the area of the trapezoid?
items.e: The parallel sides are 14 cm and 9 cm, and the height is 4 cm. A = (a + b) ÷ 2 × h = (14 + 9) ÷ 2 × 4 = 23 ÷ 2 × 4 = 11.5 × 4 = 46 cm². Do not forget to divide by 2.

items.q: What is the area of the trapezoid?
items.e: The parallel sides are 7 mm and 3 mm, and the height is 6 mm. A = (a + b) ÷ 2 × h = (7 + 3) ÷ 2 × 6 = 10 ÷ 2 × 6 = 5 × 6 = 30 mm². Do not forget to divide by 2.

items.q: What is the area of the trapezoid?
items.e: The parallel sides are 13 m and 7 m, and the height is 4 m. A = (a + b) ÷ 2 × h = (13 + 7) ÷ 2 × 4 = 20 ÷ 2 × 4 = 10 × 4 = 40 m². The 5 m side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the trapezoid?
items.e: The parallel sides are 9 cm and 3 cm, and the height is 4 cm. A = (a + b) ÷ 2 × h = (9 + 3) ÷ 2 × 4 = 12 ÷ 2 × 4 = 6 × 4 = 24 cm². The 5 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: A trapezoid has an area of 84 cm² and a height of 7 cm. One parallel side is 15 cm. How long is the other one?
items.e: 84 ÷ 7 = 12, so the two parallel sides average 12 cm. Together they are 12 × 2 = 24 cm. The other side is 24 − 15 = 9 cm. Check: (15 + 9) ÷ 2 × 7 = 84.

items.q: Which expression gives the area of the trapezoid?
items.e: Add the two parallel sides, divide by 2, then multiply by the height: (16 + 8) ÷ 2 × 3 = 36 m². The 5 m side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the trapezoid?
items.e: The parallel sides are 14 m and 5 m, and the height is 8 m. A = (a + b) ÷ 2 × h = (14 + 5) ÷ 2 × 8 = 19 ÷ 2 × 8 = 9.5 × 8 = 76 m². Do not forget to divide by 2.

items.q: Two copies of a trapezoid with parallel sides of 9 cm and 5 cm fit together to make a parallelogram. How long is the base of that parallelogram?
items.e: Turn the second copy upside down and put it beside the first. The base is 9 + 5 = 14 cm. The trapezoid is half of the parallelogram, so A = (9 + 5) × h ÷ 2, which is the same as (a + b) ÷ 2 × h.

items.q: The dashed diagonal cuts the trapezoid into two triangles. What is its area?
items.e: Bottom triangle: 16 × 8 ÷ 2 = 128 ÷ 2 = 64 cm². Top triangle (base 9 cm, same height): 9 × 8 ÷ 2 = 72 ÷ 2 = 36 cm². Add: 64 + 36 = 100 cm². Check with the formula: (16 + 9) ÷ 2 × 8 = 25 ÷ 2 × 8 = 12.5 × 8 = 100.

items.q: The dashed diagonal cuts the trapezoid into two triangles. What is its area?
items.e: Bottom triangle: 15 × 4 ÷ 2 = 60 ÷ 2 = 30 m². Top triangle (base 9 m, same height): 9 × 4 ÷ 2 = 36 ÷ 2 = 18 m². Add: 30 + 18 = 48 m². Check with the formula: (15 + 9) ÷ 2 × 4 = 24 ÷ 2 × 4 = 12 × 4 = 48.

items.q: A trapezoid has parallel sides of 12 m and 7.5 m. The height is 4 m. What is its area?
items.e: A = (a + b) ÷ 2 × h = (12 + 7.5) ÷ 2 × 4 = 19.5 ÷ 2 × 4 = 9.75 × 4 = 39 m². Add the parallel sides first, then halve, then multiply by the height.

items.q: The dashed line splits the figure into two rectangles. What is the area of the figure?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 6 × 7 = 42 and 5 × 3 = 15. Add: 42 + 15 = 57 m². Use each part of the figure once: 6 × 7 + 11 × 3 = 75 counts the 6 × 3 corner twice.

items.q: What is the area of the figure?
items.e: Rectangle: 12 × 10 = 120 cm². Triangle: its base is the 10 cm side and its height is 4 cm, so 10 × 4 ÷ 2 = 40 ÷ 2 = 20 cm². Add: 120 + 20 = 140 cm².

items.q: A triangle is cut off the corner of a rectangle (grey dashed lines). What is the area of the shaded figure?
items.e: Whole rectangle: 8 × 7 = 56 cm². Cut-off right triangle: 4 × 3 ÷ 2 = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm². Subtract: 56 − 6 = 50 cm².

items.q: What is the area of the figure? Find the two missing side lengths first.
items.e: Missing sides: 13 − 7 = 6 and 9 − 4 = 5. Whole rectangle 13 × 9 = 117, minus the missing corner 6 × 5 = 30: 117 − 30 = 87 m².

items.q: The figure is a rectangle with a triangle on top. What is its area?
items.e: Rectangle: 8 × 9 = 72 m². Triangle: 8 × 5 ÷ 2 = 40 ÷ 2 = 20 m². Add: 72 + 20 = 92 m².

items.q: What is the area of the figure?
items.e: Rectangle: 8 × 10 = 80 cm². Triangle: its base is the 10 cm side and its height is 4 cm, so 10 × 4 ÷ 2 = 40 ÷ 2 = 20 cm². Add: 80 + 20 = 100 cm².

items.q: The figure is a rectangle with a triangle on top. What is its area?
items.e: Rectangle: 6 × 10 = 60 mm². Triangle: 6 × 6 ÷ 2 = 36 ÷ 2 = 18 mm². Add: 60 + 18 = 78 mm².

items.q: What is the area of the figure?
items.e: Whole rectangle 16 × 10 = 160, minus the missing corner 7 × 6 = 42: 160 − 42 = 118 mm². Or: split it into two rectangles: 9 × 10 = 90 and 7 × 4 = 28. Add: 90 + 28 = 118 mm².

items.q: A triangle is cut off the corner of a rectangle (grey dashed lines). What is the area of the shaded figure?
items.e: Whole rectangle: 14 × 8 = 112 cm². Cut-off right triangle: 3 × 4 ÷ 2 = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm². Subtract: 112 − 6 = 106 cm².

items.q: The dashed line splits the figure into two rectangles. What is the area of the figure?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 4 × 9 = 36 and 6 × 4 = 24. Add: 36 + 24 = 60 cm². Use each part of the figure once: 4 × 9 + 10 × 4 = 76 counts the 4 × 4 corner twice.

items.q: What is the area of the figure? Find the two missing side lengths first.
items.e: Missing sides: 15 − 8 = 7 and 9 − 5 = 4. Whole rectangle 15 × 9 = 135, minus the missing corner 7 × 4 = 28: 135 − 28 = 107 cm².

items.q: What is the area of the figure?
items.e: Rectangle: 13 × 8 = 104 mm². Triangle: its base is the 8 mm side and its height is 6 mm, so 8 × 6 ÷ 2 = 48 ÷ 2 = 24 mm². Add: 104 + 24 = 128 mm².

items.q: The hexagon is a rectangle with two equal triangles. What is its area?
items.e: Rectangle: 9 × 10 = 90 mm². Each triangle: base 10 mm, height 5 mm, so 10 × 5 ÷ 2 = 50 ÷ 2 = 25 mm². Total: 90 + 25 + 25 = 140 mm².

items.q: The hexagon is a rectangle with two equal triangles. What is its area?
items.e: Rectangle: 10 × 8 = 80 m². Each triangle: base 8 m, height 5 m, so 8 × 5 ÷ 2 = 40 ÷ 2 = 20 m². Total: 80 + 20 + 20 = 120 m².

items.q: The figure is a rectangle with a triangle on top. What is its area?
items.e: The triangle is 9 − 5 = 4 cm tall. Rectangle: 14 × 5 = 70 cm². Triangle: 14 × 4 ÷ 2 = 56 ÷ 2 = 28 cm². Add: 70 + 28 = 98 cm².

items.q: What is the area of the figure?
items.e: Whole rectangle 16 × 10 = 160, minus the missing corner 9 × 6 = 54: 160 − 54 = 106 cm². Or: split it into two rectangles: 7 × 10 = 70 and 9 × 4 = 36. Add: 70 + 36 = 106 cm².

items.q: The dashed line splits the figure into a rectangle and a triangle. What is its area?
items.e: Rectangle: 7 × 8 = 56 m². The triangle’s base is 12 − 7 = 5 m and its height is 8 m: 5 × 8 ÷ 2 = 40 ÷ 2 = 20 m². Add: 56 + 20 = 76 m².

items.q: A triangle is cut off the corner of a rectangle (grey dashed lines). What is the area of the shaded figure?
items.e: Whole rectangle: 14 × 7 = 98 m². Cut-off right triangle: 4 × 3 ÷ 2 = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 m². Subtract: 98 − 6 = 92 m².

items.q: The figure is a rectangle with a triangle on top. What is its area?
items.e: The triangle is 14 − 10 = 4 cm tall. Rectangle: 14 × 10 = 140 cm². Triangle: 14 × 4 ÷ 2 = 56 ÷ 2 = 28 cm². Add: 140 + 28 = 168 cm².

items.q: The dashed line splits the figure into a rectangle and a triangle. What is its area?
items.e: Rectangle: 7 × 7 = 49 cm². The triangle’s base is 10 − 7 = 3 cm and its height is 7 cm: 3 × 7 ÷ 2 = 21 ÷ 2 = 10.5 cm². Add: 49 + 10.5 = 59.5 cm².

sets.title: Word problems: gardens, sails and flags

items.q: Sofia stains a cedar deck in Nanaimo shaped like a trapezoid. The parallel sides are 5 m and 3 m, and the height is 4 m. Stain costs $6 per square metre. How much does the stain cost?
A triangular flower bed has a base of 8 m and a height of 5 m. One packet of wildflower seeds covers 4 m². How many packets are needed for the whole bed?
The front wall of a ski cabin in Whistler is a rectangle 8 m wide and 3 m tall with a triangle on top that is 2 m tall. What is the area of the wall?
items.e: Rectangle: 8 × 3 = 24 m². Triangle: 8 × 2 ÷ 2 = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 m². Total: 24 + 8 = 32 m². (40 forgets to divide the triangle by 2.)

items.q: A backyard rink in Prince George is an L-shape: a 12 m by 8 m rectangle with a 4 m by 3 m corner left out for a shed. What is the area of the ice?
items.e: Whole rectangle: 12 × 8 = 96 m². Corner: 4 × 3 = 12 m². Ice: 96 − 12 = 84 m².

items.q: Noah’s class makes 20 triangular flags for a Terry Fox Run banner. Each flag has a base of 30 cm and a height of 45 cm. How much fabric do the flags use in all?
items.e: One flag: 30 × 45 ÷ 2 = 1350 ÷ 2 = 675 cm². Twenty flags: 20 × 675 = 13 500 cm².

items.q: A triangular sail has sides of 10 m, 17 m and 21 m. The height to the 21 m side is 8 m. What is its area?
items.e: Use the 21 m side as the base and the 8 m height: A = 21 × 8 ÷ 2 = 168 ÷ 2 = 84 m². The 10 m and 17 m sides are slanted, so they are not the height.

items.q: Triangle A has a base of 10 cm and a height of 8 cm. Parallelogram B has a base of 5 cm and a height of 8 cm. Which is true?
c: A is twice as large as B.
items.e: A: 10 × 8 ÷ 2 = 80 ÷ 2 = 40 cm². B: 5 × 8 = 40 cm². Same area. (Forgetting the ÷ 2 makes A look twice as large.)

items.q: A park in Victoria is a rectangle 80 m long and 60 m wide. It has a triangular pond with a base of 20 m and a height of 15 m. The rest of the park is grass. What is the area of the grass?
A corner lot in Kamloops is a right triangle. Its sides along the two streets are 30 m and 40 m, and the back side is 50 m. What is the area of the lot?
items.e: The two street sides meet at a right angle, so they are the base and the height. A = 30 × 40 ÷ 2 = 1200 ÷ 2 = 600 m². The 50 m side is slanted.

items.q: Ethan’s family plants a vegetable garden in Kelowna shaped like a parallelogram. Its base is 8 m and its height is 5 m. The slanted sides are 6 m long. What is the area of the garden?
items.e: A = base × height = 8 × 5 = 40 m². The 6 m sides are slanted, so they are not the height.

items.q: A school garden bed in Surrey is a trapezoid. Its parallel sides are 6 m and 4 m, and the height is 3 m. What is its area?
Mateo’s family lays a path with 25 patio stones shaped like parallelograms. Each stone has a base of 40 cm, a height of 30 cm and slanted sides of 35 cm. What area do the stones cover?
items.e: One stone: 40 × 30 = 1200 cm². 25 stones: 25 × 1200 = 30 000 cm². The 35 cm sides are slanted, so they are not the height.

items.q: Students paint a mural on a wall shaped like a trapezoid. The parallel sides are 9 m and 7 m, and the height is 5 m. One can of paint covers 10 m². How many cans do they need?

A parking space at a SkyTrain station is a parallelogram. It is 2.5 m wide along the curb, and its painted slanted lines are 6 m long. The distance straight back from the curb is 5.5 m. What is its area?
items.e: A = base × height = 2.5 × 5.5 = 13.75 m². The 6 m lines are slanted, so they are not the height.

items.q: A community garden in Burnaby is shaped like a parallelogram. Its area is 1200 m² and its base is 40 m. What is its height?
items.e: Area = base × height, so 40 × h = 1200. h = 1200 ÷ 40 = 30 m. (Halving is only for triangles.)

items.q: Kai’s canoe club makes 15 triangular pennants. Each pennant has a base of 24 cm and a height of 40 cm. How much fabric do the pennants use in all?
items.e: One pennant: 24 × 40 ÷ 2 = 960 ÷ 2 = 480 cm². Fifteen pennants: 15 × 480 = 7200 cm².

items.q: A lacrosse team flag is a rectangle 90 cm long and 60 cm tall. A red triangle on the flag has the 60 cm side as its base and reaches 45 cm into the flag. The rest is white. What is the area of the white part?
items.e: Flag: 90 × 60 = 5400 cm². Triangle: 60 × 45 ÷ 2 = 2700 ÷ 2 = 1350 cm². White part: 5400 − 1350 = 4050 cm². (5400 − 2700 forgets to divide by 2.)

items.q: A wooden trail sign on Grouse Mountain is a rectangle 60 cm long and 20 cm tall with a triangle on one end, like an arrow. The triangle’s base is the 20 cm side, and it sticks out 15 cm. What is the area of the sign?
items.e: Rectangle: 60 × 20 = 1200 cm². Triangle: 20 × 15 ÷ 2 = 300 ÷ 2 = 150 cm². Total: 1200 + 150 = 1350 cm².

items.q: A triangular sail has an area of 12 m². Its base is 4 m. How tall is the sail?
A small sailboat on English Bay in Vancouver has a sail shaped like a right triangle. The bottom edge is 3 m, the edge along the mast is 4 m and the slanted edge is 5 m. What is the area of the sail?
items.e: The bottom edge and the mast meet at a right angle, so they are the base and the height. A = 3 × 4 ÷ 2 = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 m². The 5 m edge is slanted.
